intro: A band billed as bingo.
story: Kevin Richey, who goes by Bingo, played banjo and co-fronted the Portland bluegrass and old-time band Golden Delicious with Pete Krebs. The band formed in the mid 1990s and drew a loyal local crowd with high-energy acoustic shows that mixed bluegrass, swing, country and folk. Cavity Search Records released its records, Old School in 1997, Cavity Search in 1998 and Live at the Laurelthirst in 1999, the year bingo was on the first Pickathon bill.

intro: A Portland songwriter leading his own trio.
story: Casey Neill's trio made Skree in 1999, its only studio album, produced by Johnny Cunningham, and it played Pickathon in 2000. A live disc followed and the trio disbanded. He later made Memory Against Forgetting in 2005 and Brooklyn Bridge in 2007, which No Depression called career-defining and which belongs to New York as much as Portland. Casey Neill & the Norway Rats returned with Subterrene in 2022, their first album in five years, then Sending Up Flares in fall 2023, and his solo record time zero land came out in July 2024.

intro: A Portland country-rock band fronted by Elisabeth Ames.
story: Elisabeth Ames formed the Countrypolitans with Coleman of the Freddy Trujillo band as a home for their shared love of roots music, and the band played Pickathon in 2000. Ames cites Merle Haggard and Patsy Cline, and guitarist Hershel Yatovitz of Chris Isaak's band has sat in with them. The band now plays as Elisabeth Ames and the Countrypolitans, and in March 2025 Pickathon presented a Two-Step Tuesday with them at the Showdown in Portland.

intro: A Portland country and rock band.
story: The Freak Mountain Ramblers grew out of the rhythm section of the Holy Modal Rounders after that group landed in Portland, and they played Pickathon in 2000. Bassist David Reisch later recalled that the name came from a remark about the hills near Plainview, west of Portland, and that Billy Kennedy gave them the use of it. The Oregon Music Hall of Fame inducted the band on October 13, 2018, and it ended in January 2016. A live video of them playing Buckets of Rain in 1999 is posted on Vortex.

intro: A bassist from Leftover Salmon's slamgrass years.
story: Tye North played bass in Leftover Salmon from 1993 to 2000, the band that billed its sound as polyethnic Cajun slamgrass, and he announced he was leaving after the Planet Salmon Fest that September to pursue his own music. A jam supergroup, Theory of Everything, debuted at the Boulder Theater on September 7, 2000, with North, Dave Watts, Ross Martin, Michael Kang and Kyle Hollingsworth. After leaving he toured with the Portland funk band Porterhouse in fall 2001, recorded with Keller Williams on Laugh, and subbed for the bass player in Michael Hurley's band. He also played with Danny Barnes and assembled his own trio.

intro: A Portland mandolinist and his bluegrass band.
story: Caleb Klauder's bluegrass band played Pickathon in 2001, and its music soundtracked a Food Network trip through Portland the next year. Klauder and Sammy Lind have played together since 2000, when the first version of Foghorn Stringband formed, and both were steeped in old-time music before that. Klauder went on to lead Foghorn, and the Caleb Klauder Country Band made Dangerous Me's and Poisonous You's and Western Country before its first Mountain Stage appearance in April 2012.

intro: A Vancouver Celtic-bluegrass rock band.
story: The Clumsy Lovers came together in Vancouver in 1993 from the original lineup of the Paperboys, and they were a touring band by 2001, playing more than 270 shows in 2002. They self-released a run of albums between 2000 and 2002 and were mainly a live band until Nettwerk Records signed them and released After the Flood, their first studio album for a label. Smart Kid followed in June 2005. The band has since counted more than 2,500 performances.

intro: A Portland bluegrass quartet.
story: Jackstraw, a Portland bluegrass quartet, began when Darrin Craig, David Pugh, Jon Neufeld and Jesse Withers met at a Portland music store and started making music together in 1997. They were on the 2001 bill and have come back more often than most bands, through 2022.

intro: A Bay Area bluegrass singer, fiddler and songwriter.
story: Laurie Lewis, whose "Who Will Watch the Home Place" was the IBMA's song of the year in 1994, played Pickathon in 2001 with Tom Rozum. Her album Laurie Lewis and Her Bluegrass Pals came out on Rounder in 1999, recorded in Menlo Park. The Hazel and Alice Sessions, with the Right Hands, was nominated for the 2017 Grammy for Best Bluegrass Album, and O California!, her 25th album, came out in February 2026.

intro: A Portland bluegrass band.
story: Pig Iron was a Portland old-time string band with Caleb Klauder on mandolin and Taylor Grover on banjo, and it played Pickathon in 2001. The band made one album, Fill Me Up, in 1999. Klauder, who went on to lead Foghorn Stringband, lists it among the bands he toured with early on, alongside Colobo.

intro: A Portland acoustic blues guitarist.
story: Terry Robb, who befriended John Fahey in the early 1980s and later produced and played on most of Fahey's late albums, signed with Portland's Burnside Records in 1994. Heart Made of Steel came out in June 2000, recorded at Poundhouse Studios in Portland, and he played Pickathon in 2001, followed by When I Play My Blues Guitar in 2002. In 2024 he made CrissCross, a duo album with the Canadian blues pianist David Vest on Cordova Bay Records, produced by the two of them.

intro: A Seattle circus and cabaret troupe.
story: Circus Contraption, a Seattle one-ring circus and dark cabaret troupe founded in 1998, brought its band to Pickathon in 2002. It had recorded the CD Gallimaufry in 2001 with a Jack Straw Artist Support Program grant, and Our Latest Catalogue came out on June 14, 2002. Kevin Hinshaw led the music, and The Stranger ranked the troupe among the best of the new cabaret movement for its look, its physical skill and its musicianship. It disbanded in 2009 and issued The Show to End All Shows in 2010.

intro: A Portland old-time band.
story: Foghorn Stringband began when its founding members met at the National Oldtime Fiddlers' Contest in Weiser, Idaho, in 2000, under the name Foghorn Leghorn. It played Pickathon in 2002, the first of eight visits through 2016. From 2009 to 2011 it ran as a full string band, with Patrick Lind and Peter Leone beside Caleb Klauder and Nadine Landry, and Reeb Willms joined in 2011. Outshine the Sun came out in 2012 and Devil in the Seat in 2015, and in March 2020 the band toured the East Coast, with Landry and Lind coming from Quebec and Willms and Klauder from Portland.

intro: A Portland junkbox blues duo.
story: Hillstomp, the Portland duo of Henry Kammerer on guitar and vocals and John Johnson on buckets and a junk kit, met in 2001 and built a North Mississippi-style hill country blues stomp. They played Pickathon in 2004, a year before their debut, One Word, came out in March 2005. Willamette Week named their next record, The Woman That Ended the World, its best local album of 2005. Portland, Ore., their first new record since 2010, came out on Fluff & Gravy in 2014 and Monster Receiver in 2018, and their music turned up in the third season of Sons of Anarchy.

intro: An Iowa folk singer with a gravel baritone.
story: Greg Brown, the Iowa folk singer born in Ottumwa in 1949, has been active since 1967. His first record was Hacklebarney in 1974, a duo album with Richard Pinney, and he self-released 44 & 66 in 1980 and The Iowa Waltz in 1981, before Red House put out In the Dark with You in 1983. He played Pickathon in 2006, the year The Evening Call came out. He has two Grammy nominations for Best Traditional Folk Album, one for Friend of Mine, shared with Bill Morrissey, and one for Slant 6 Mind. In 2010 he sang the part of Hades on Anais Mitchell's folk opera Hadestown. His last studio album was Hymns to What Is Left in 2012, he stopped touring in 2019 and played two final shows in 2023, and the songbook Ring Around the Moon was published in April 2024.

intro: A Portland bluegrass quartet with a honky-tonk edge.
story: Jackstraw, the Portland bluegrass quartet, began in 1997 when Darrin Craig, David Pugh, Jon Neufeld and Jesse Withers started making music together after meeting at a Portland music store. They played Pickathon in 2001, 2003, 2005 and 2007, and returned in 2009, 2013 and 2022. Their self-titled album came out in 2003 and Live at the White Eagle, recorded in September 2004, in 2005. Sunday Never Comes, their sixth album, arrived in April 2012 with banjo player Cory Goldman.

intro: Portland's all-woman old-time string band.
story: Flat Mountain Girls, a Portland old-time string band that began in 2001 when Rachel Gold and a bandmate met after both were new to the city, played Pickathon in 2007. The lineup was Lisa Marsicek on fiddle, Rachel Gold on banjo, Nann Alleman on guitar and Arthur Parker on bass, and the band released albums in 2003 and 2005, the second of them Honey Take Your Whiskers Off. Their third album, Idle Talk & Wicked Deeds, came out on May 23 that year. No Depression profiled them as postmodern traditionalists and called the new album a perfect distillation of the band. It became a local favorite on the Northwest square-dance and festival circuit.

intro: A Portland bluegrass band, here for the sixth time.
story: Jackstraw are a Portland bluegrass quartet, playing together since 1997 and known for a gritty, honky-tonk-inflected sound. Their guitarist said in a 2012 interview that they had played nearly every Pickathon since the festival began, and by 2013 they were back for the sixth time, after 2001, 2003, 2005, 2007 and 2009. They came again in 2022, and have stayed loyal to home, recently playing a Portland FolkMusic Society show.

intro: A Richmond harmonica player in the Chicago style.
story: Andrew Alli is a Richmond, Virginia blues harmonica player who works in the Chicago style. He played Pickathon in 2018, and The Bluegrass Situation premiered a live session from the Lucky Barn, his song My Stomp with Josh Small. In 2021 he was honored in the Living Blues critics' poll, and he has kept playing blues festivals since, including Helen Harp Fest in Georgia.

intro: A New Orleans Mardi Gras Indian group, played as funk.
story: 79rs Gang is a New Orleans group in the Mardi Gras Indian tradition, led by Big Chiefs Romeo Bougere and Jermaine Bossier, who play it as funk, with drums and chants. Expect the Unexpected came out in 2020. They played Pickathon in 2022, and later that year KEXP filmed their set at Trans Musicales in Rennes, France. Into 2025 they kept playing Tipitina's, the New Orleans club, on Mardi Gras weekend.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 6 pm, Grove · Sun Aug 7, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: A Portland bluegrass band with honky-tonk in it.
story: Jackstraw is a Portland bluegrass band, playing together since 1997, with a honky-tonk edge. They have played Pickathon more times than almost anyone, and their 2022 set was the seventh. They still play Portland stages and the Portland FolkMusic Society's shows.
sets: Thu Aug 4, 9 pm, Galaxy Barn · Fri Aug 5, 6 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: Four Vancouver songwriters in close harmony.
story: The Breakmen, four Vancouver songwriters who formed the band in 2005, brought tight, harmony-driven acoustic music to Pickathon in 2007; the live track Town Changes from that set came out on Pickathon's Bandcamp in October 2008. Heartwood came out in 2010, and members later moved on to other Canadian roots projects.
